story_sequence.text: Beacon freezes a `Skill Anatomy v2` baseline for key host-visible skills with explicit sections for usage boundary, workflow or decision loop, rationalization risk, verification, evidence, state, and gate semantics.

`using-beacon`, `beacon-prd`, `beacon-change`, `beacon-brainstorm`, `beacon-implement`, `beacon-qa`, and `beacon-release` all include explicit anti-rationalization guidance instead of relying on implied operator discipline.

Beacon defines one unified support-surface constitution for `brainstorm`, `deep`, `ceo-review`, `design-review`, `help`, `status`, and `doctor`, and that constitution preserves `not truth source`, `not gate source`, and `not new lifecycle stage`.

high-risk challenge output is formalized so review-style surfaces can challenge decisions, but the result must map back to route, evidence, state, or gate impact instead of ending as free-form commentary.
Beacon formalizes a public surface family model that distinguishes truth surfaces, execution surfaces, support surfaces, and gate surfaces with clear escalation and handoff boundaries.
machine-checkable anti-drift enforcement is defined for the new contract baseline so missing sections, overreaching support surfaces, or unbound challenge outputs can be detected automatically.
the v1.4.6 contract preserves Beacon's philosophy-first skill design and does not regress into step-by-step operation scripts for strong models.
Beacon absorbs external workflow-skill methods as internal contract design, anti-rationalization, and orchestration patterns without creating a runtime dependency on external skill packs.
`brainstorm` and `change` remain distinct: `brainstorm` can sharpen options and framing, but only `change` can promote requirement truth intended for downstream implementation and QA.
the new anti-drift contract is documented as a host-visible behavior upgrade for Beacon rather than a new lifecycle stage or a replacement for existing truth, evidence, and gate governance.
